case_text:
Vignette:
A 22-year-old woman with type 1 diabetes diagnosed at age 8 presents with 2 days of worsening nausea, vomiting, diffuse abdominal pain, and progressive lethargy. She reports that she ran out of insulin 3 days ago and could not afford a refill. On examination, she is drowsy but arousable, markedly dehydrated with dry mucous membranes and poor skin turgor. Vital signs: T 36.4C, HR 128, RR 32 (deep, labored Kussmaul respirations), BP 92/54, SpO2 99%. Her breath has a distinct fruity acetone odor. Abdomen is diffusely tender without peritoneal signs. Labs: glucose 486 mg/dL, pH 7.08, pCO2 14 mmHg, bicarbonate 4 mEq/L, anion gap 32, beta-hydroxybutyrate 8.2 mmol/L, potassium 5.6 mEq/L (expected to drop with treatment), sodium 128 mEq/L (corrected 134), BUN 38 mg/dL, creatinine 1.9 mg/dL.
